jobs.occupation: Financial Controller
jobs.description:
We’re looking for an experienced Financial Controller to take full ownership of our numbers as we scale. You’ll run a tight month-end close, get our SaaS revenue accounting airtight, and build the finance processes that let us grow fast without drowning in manual work. If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

About Pandektes

Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

We’re still early in the journey, and joining our team now means you’ll have big impact on shaping how we scale.

About the role

This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, overseeing the month-end close, management accounts, financial reporting and statutory compliance, while continuously improving financial processes, systems and internal controls and working closely with Senior Management, external service providers and the wider business teams. The role will combine strong technical accounting expertise with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

What you’ll do

• 
Own the monthly and annual close – reviewing journals, accruals, prepayments, provisions and balance sheet reconciliations, and delivering accurate trial balances and financial statements on time

• 
Make sure our SaaS revenue (subscription, usage-based and implementation) is recognised correctly, and reconcile revenue schedules to billing, contracts and the general ledger

• 
Produce reliable monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting

• 
Take over revenue billing from the sales team and run it within finance

• 
Manage our outsourced service providers and review the reconciliations they prepare – bank, intercompany, payroll, fixed assets and other control accounts

• 
Design and maintain financial policies, controls and approval limits across payments, expenses, procurement and system access

• 
Oversee AP, AR and cashbook accounting, manage payments through Corepay, and keep an eye on working capital

• 
Lead statutory accounts and external audits, and oversee VAT, corporate tax and compliance with our tax advisers

• 
Coordinate intercompany accounting and reporting across our entities in Denmark, Germany, Switzerland and the UK

• 
Improve finance processes, systems and automation – and over time, build and develop a small accounting team

What you’ll bring

• 
7+ years in commercially focused accounting roles, ideally with previous experience as a Financial Controller

• 
A recognised Danish accounting qualification (or equivalent, e.g. ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

• 
Hands-on experience with subscription and deferred revenue, including month-end revenue reconciliations

• 
A track record of independently running the month-end close and producing accurate management accounts

• 
Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

• 
Exposure to international tax, VAT and transfer pricing, and experience running a local audit process

• 
A strong grasp of internal controls, segregation of duties and fraud risk

• 
Experience improving finance operations in a growing, scaling business – and a love for systems and automation

• 
A sharp eye for detail and the analytical instinct to tell a real business issue from an accounting error

How we work

We place great value on a vibrant, inspiring, and challenging company culture. This is achieved through a talented and passionate team that believes in achieving great things together.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We believe that ownership is what brings us the best teams – you can expect a lot of freedom and responsibility. The key is open communication, trust, and a shared passion to transform the legal world.

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

What we offer

• 
Competitive compensation + an attractive warrant program

• 
A collaborative work environment where your input is not only valued but often implemented within hours

• 
A central office in Copenhagen, where you can work closely with an ambitious and growing team

• 
International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

• 
25 vacation days per year + public holidays

• 
Your own Pleo card for necessary work expenses

• 
Paid parental leave

Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

jobs.occupation: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
The company

Our client is a venture-backed Copenhagen biotech that designs a new class of oral drugs. It uses its own generative AI, automated chemistry and high-throughput biology. The platform has made and tested hundreds of thousands of novel compounds, and the company has a major pharma partnership behind it. R&D is organised under a CTO across three groups: AI & Computational Drug Design, Platform Chemistry, and Screening Biology.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will own the company's internal scientific software, so every team works from the same clean, consistent data with tools that fit together.

The company creates, moves and decides on large volumes of chemistry and biology data. Today each team builds its own solutions. The company is moving to a new data platform built for its molecules and will build custom internal products on top of it.

The Product Manager is the person who sees that three teams are building three versions of the same thing and turns them into one that works for everyone. Success is measured in time saved for the scientists: the software should save more than it costs.

Responsibilities

Product ownership

• Owns the roadmap for the internal scientific software, starting with the three products above.

• Gathers and challenges requirements from computational design, chemistry and biology, and turns parallel requests into shared solutions.

• Prioritises with the leadership team: what gets built, in what order, and why.

• Makes sure the products connect to each other and to the data platform.

• Runs user testing and adoption with the scientists, and tracks the time saved.

Delivery and leadership

• Works agile, and knows where agility stops. Ships working products within months without painting the platform into a corner.

• Leads and coordinates 3–6 developers, a mix of contractors and hires. A front-end engineer may report directly.

• Helps shape the software team as it grows.

Hands-on, at the start

• Contributes to the build until the development team is in place. The stack is Python on the back end, React/Redux on the front end, and AWS serverless services.

• Judges which components fit together and which will break, including AI-assisted code.

The profile

The ideal candidate has experience from an environment where software is built and shipped, and a scientific background. Beyond that, in order of importance:

• People leadership. Has led developers or cross-functional teams, internal or contracted, and aligned stakeholders who don't report to them.

• Product management track record. Has owned a software product or platform from idea to adoption.

• Drug discovery experience. Has worked close to design, synthesis, screening or compound selection. Broader R&D software is also relevant.

• Scientific background. A chemistry or biology degree (either is fine). Knows what they don't know, and asks.

• Hands-on coding. Can build in Python and React. Judgement matters more than depth.

Mindset: curious enough to ask "what's a canonical SMILES?", pragmatic about agile, and happy to start hands-on and grow into leading a team.

Nice to have: AWS serverless, lab automation or screening data, ELN/LIMS or compound registration, startup or scale-up experience. The working language is English.

Set-up, package and process

• Reporting. To the VP of AI & Computational Drug Design, with a weekly 1:1 and short daily stand-ups.

• Location. On site in Copenhagen, enough to work alongside the chemists and biologists in the lab. There is no fixed number of days.

• Career path. Starts senior and hands-on, and grows into leading a dedicated software team.

• Package. A competitive salary, pension, a performance bonus, and participation in the company's warrant programme.

• Process. A short screening call, then an online session where the candidate presents software they have built, then on-site interviews. The target start is early 2027.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellowship Position in Causal inference at the Section of Biostatistics and The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed
jobs.employer_name: KU - SUND - Institut For Folkesundhed - Kbh K
jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health at University of Copenhagen, Denmark, together with the The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomeds offers a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in causal inference with special focus on continuous-time causal inference, identification, and instrumental variables methods. 

  The anticipated hiring date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  About the Centre

  The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease.

  About the Section of Biostatistics
 The Section of Biostatistics carries out independent research in biostatistical applications and methods; it undertakes teaching of students at various educations, undergraduate as well as postgraduate, and it offers biostatistical advice to staff and students in all disciplines of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences. The section is internationally renowned for a high research level, especially within time-to-event analysis, while other competence areas include e.g. causal inference, latent variable modelling and prediction models. The section aims to maintain a strong position in these areas but also wants to expand into new areas of biostatistical research. The underlying idea is to produce high-level methodological research that is relevant in practical applications.

  More information on the Section of Biostatistics can be found at: https://biostat.ku.dk/. 
  

  Job Description
 We invite highly qualified, thorough, and motivated applicants to apply for a postdoctoral position in causal inference and statistical methodology. The successful candidate will conduct methodological research at the intersection of causal inference, event-history analysis, statistical machine learning, and semiparametric theory. Research will focus on the development of statistical methods for longitudinal and time-to-event data, with particular emphasis on continuously monitored data, dynamic treatment strategies, identification, and instrumental variable methods. Potential research directions include:  

   	
• causal inference for survival and competing risks outcomes 	
• continuous-time longitudinal causal models 	
• semiparametric and machine-learning-based estimation methods 	
• identification and estimation under instrumental variable assumptions 	
• methods for treatment switching, treatment discontinuation, and dynamic treatment interventions 	
• development of efficient and robust estimators for causal effects under complex longitudinal data structures   Example projects include the development of methods for causal inference with continuously observed treatment processes, incorporation of instrumental variables into survival analysis, and machine-learning-based estimation procedures for time-varying treatment effects. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute both theoretically and computationally, including development of new methodology, investigation of statistical properties, implementation of software, simulation studies, and applications to biomedical research questions. The candidate must participate in the interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment within the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed. The successful applicant is also encouraged to develop independent research directions aligned with the overall goals of the centre.

  The specific tasks of the position will include:

   	
• Manage own academic research and administrative activities. 	
• Conduct research in line with the goals of SMARTBiomed. 	
• Lead write-up of research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure, where appropriate, that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility. 	
• Present papers at conferences or public meetings. 	
• Contribute to the administrative activities of SMARTBiomed and the research group of appointment.   The postdoctoral fellow will also be encouraged and mentored to develop new proposals and research initiatives to support additional research. Over the course of the position, opportunities to teach at either the graduate or undergraduate level exist.

   

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:
 Essential experience and skills:

   	
• A Ph.D. in Statistics/Biostatistics, or similar disciplines.  	
• Strong skills in theoretical methods development.  	
• Experience and interest in data analysis and programming (e.g., in R) is further highly desirable.  	
• Strong English, scientific writing, and oral communications skills 	
• The ability to work independently, effectively, and collaboratively.    

  Terms of employment 
 The position is fixed term, limited to a period of 3 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 36,877.42 DKK/approx. 4,933.00 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Questions
 More information about the positions is available by contacting Associate Professor Helene Rytgaard, Section of Biostatistics, hely@sund.ku.dk, Professor Erin Gabriel, Section of Biostatistics, erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk, or Professor Torben Martinussen, Section of Biostatistics, tma@sund.ku.dk.   

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter indicating your motivation for application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications and archived works in progress.    

  Deadline for applications: December 1st, 2026.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery at the Department of Pharmacy
jobs.description:
We are offering a PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery commencing 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  Our group and research

  Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have revolutionized the field of nucleic acid therapeutics and are now central to the development of mRNA-based medicines. Understanding the connection between nanoparticle composition, structure, and biological performance is essential for further advances in the field. The Vaccine Design and Delivery group investigates these relationships through a combination of biophysical, structural, and analytical approaches. The group also focuses on in vitro testing, in vivo imaging of biodistribution, and in vivo immunogenicity and protection studies in animal models. The overarching goal is to enable the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will join a new research program led by Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani, an expert in advanced physicochemical methods to study lipid self-assembly. 

  Project description

  The overall aim of the PhD project is to advance the understanding of lipid nanoparticle (LNP) systems for nucleic acid delivery through the integration of formulation design, structural characterization, and interaction studies. The candidate will employ state-of-the-art biophysical and structural techniques to investigate the nanoscale structure of LNPs and their behavior in biologically relevant environments. By combining advanced nanoparticle formulation with cutting-edge characterization methods, including scattering techniques and electron microscopy, the project seeks to establish quantitative relationships between LNP composition, structure, and biological interactions. These approaches will be used to investigate how LNP properties govern interactions with biological media and membranes, generating fundamental insights that will guide the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will work under the supervision of Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani within the Vaccine Design and Delivery group. The PhD fellowship is part of a larger research project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark through a Sapere Aude: DFF-Research Leader grant.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Camilla Foged, Department of Pharmacy, camilla.foged@sund.ku.dk, Direct Phone: +45 35 33 64 02.

  Co-Supervisor is Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani, federica.sebastiani@sund.ku.dk

  Start:            1 March 2027 (or after agreement)

  Duration:     3 years as a PhD student

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent research project under supervision.    	
• Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team. 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project 	
• Teaching and disseminating your knowledge. 	
• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme Description:

  The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., Physical chemistry, Biophysics, Nanotechnology or related fields).

  The successful candidate will specifically work on 1) formulation of mRNA-LNPs; 2) investigating the structure and morphology of LNPs in the absence and presence of biomimetic fluid; 3) understanding the mechanism of interaction of LNPs with model membranes.

  The project combines a range of experimental biophysical methods, including lab-based techniques and experiments at large-scale neutron and X-ray scattering facilities in Europe.

  Qualifications:
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  Job Description
 The Perrier Lab at the Department of Neuroscience, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, is seeking a motivated and talented PhD fellow to study the impact of gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in GABAA  receptors implicated in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs).

  DEEs are severe early-onset conditions characterized by intractable epilepsy, intellectual disability, developmental delay or regression, movement disorders, and autism spectrum disorders. Although missense variants in GABAA receptor subunits are often assumed to cause loss of receptor function (LOF), recent work by our collaborators at the University of Sydney (Australia) and Filadelfia Hospital (Denmark) shows that GOF variants are just as prevalent, and their functional outcomes closely correlate with patient phenotypes.

  Project Overview
 The main goal of this project is to understand how mutations that increase inhibitory signaling in the brain can nevertheless lead to DEE. To address this, you will investigate animal models carrying GOF GABAA receptor mutations found in patients, examining their effects at multiple levels:

   	
• In Vivo  	 		
• Monitor animal behavior and record electrocorticographic (ECoG) activity to detect abnormalities linked to patient symptoms. 	 	 	
• In Vitro 	 		
• Use brain slice preparations to measure neuronal activity at the microcircuit level, comparing GOF mutants to wild-type littermates. This approach will clarify if microcircuits from the thalamocortical loop are impaired in GOF DEE models and if impairments are responsible for the epileptic phenotype. 	 	   Based on these findings, you will contribute to the design and testing of targeted treatments aimed at correcting the underlying defects, first in vitro and subsequently in vivo. This project will be conducted in close collaboration with Filadelfia Hospital, which maintains a cohort of patients affected by these rare and severe conditions.

You will be involved in collaborations with researchers in agricultural and environmental economics as well as researchers in other disciplines and stakeholders collaborating in the same project.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in Environmental or Agricultural Economics or similar. Candidates should demonstrate strong skills in quantitative economics methods. Documented experience with farm economics and biodiversity is desirable.

The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technology at Aarhus University. Department of Public Health
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

Do you have a strong methodological foundation and an interest in designing, analysing and interpreting epidemiological observational studies? Do you enjoy working with large-scale datasets from national registries and cohort studies to address important public health questions? And would you like to contribute to research with high societal relevance, focusing on health and development from early childhood to adulthood?

If so, we invite you to apply for a full-time position (37 hours/week) as Staff Scientist in the Perinatal, Obstetric & Paediatric Epidemiology (POPE) Group at the Section of Epidemiology, University of Copenhagen, starting 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. In this role, you will execute analytical tasks within epidemiological research projects using national registry and cohort data, while developing and maintaining research data resources.

About Section of Epidemiology and the POPE group 

The Section of Epidemiology conducts research on determinants of health and disease across the life-course, with the aim of improving public health and advancing epidemiological theory.

You will join the POPE group, whose research focuses on maternal, child, and adolescent health from a life-course perspective. Our work examines how perinatal and early childhood exposures influence health outcomes throughout childhood and into young adulthood. Research topics include preterm birth, infections and vaccinations during pregnancy, mental health, and psychiatric treatment. The POPE group extensively uses Danish registry data and the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC), which provides rich self-reported and biological data. DNBC is a nationwide birth cohort including more than 96,000 individuals born in 1996-2003 whose mothers enrolled during pregnancy – more details here. The group is deeply involved in ongoing and future DNBC data collections, long-term follow-up, and international cohort collaborations. For more details read here: POPE

About the Department
The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

About the Position
The Staff Scientist will play a central role in advancing and executing epidemiological research within the POPE group. Working collaboratively with researchers, external collaborators, and colleagues across the Department of Public Health, with opportunities of conducting independent research, while the primary responsibility is to contribute and execute projects led by others based on large-scale Danish registry and cohort data. Responsibilities will include developing and maintaining research data resources, ensuring rigorous data quality, performing advanced analytical and statistical workflows, and contributing to the establishment/maintenance of data infrastructures that enable high-quality epidemiological research and peer-reviewed publications. The tasks include:

• 
Developing, maintaining, and quality assuring large-scale epidemiological data resources based on Danish national registries and cohort data including the DNBC.

• 
Contributing to the design, implementation, and conduct of epidemiological research projects by preparing analytical datasets, performing descriptive and statistical analyses, and supporting the interpretation and dissemination of findings.

• 
Coordinating key research activities related to the DNBC, including the ongoing 25-year follow-up and international federated analyses across cohorts.

• 
Establishing data set-ups where cohort data are embedded within register-based populations for resources beyond DNBC

• 
Providing methodological and analytical support to a broad range of epidemiological research projects within the group, contributing expertise in study implementation, data handling, troubleshooting and project development as needed.

• 
Taking responsibility for data security, exportation of analysis results, data governance and GDPR compliance within the POPE group

Profile and Qualifications

• 
Preferably a PhD in epidemiology and/or, public health or related fields.

• 
Advanced methodological and analytical skills, including demonstrated experience with data management, study design, statistical modelling, and interpretation of observational epidemiological data.

• 
A proven ability to envision, plan, and execute epidemiological research projects independently, while delivering work to agreed deadlines.

• 
Proven experience working with large and complex datasets from Danish national registries, large cohorts, or other longitudinal data sources using R, STATA and/or SAS.

• 
Strong scientific writing skills, with a track record of preparing and publishing peer-reviewed publications and project documentation.

• 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide expert methodological guidance and explain complex findings to researchers from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative fashion.

• 
Fluency in Danish (both written and spoken) is required, as the role involves working extensively with Danish national registry data and documentation.

• 
Experience in, or a strong interest in perinatal and life-course epidemiology, including research on child development, adolescent health, and/or mental health.

As a PhD student, you will investigate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment of dikes, accounting for uncertainties in soil characterisation through modelling. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with slope stability analysis, statistical methods, physical modelling and risk assessment while addressing one of the pressing challenges of climate change in the built environment. 

You will become part of an ambitious and highly interdisciplinary research environment at DTU Sustain, collaborating closely with the Center for Coasts and Climate Adaptation, The Danish Environmental Protection Agency (formerly Danish Coastal Directorate) and Ghent University, while benefiting from access to state-of-the-art facilities in soil mechanics, geotechnical engineering and physical modelling. The position also includes international research stays with our collaborators, providing opportunities to develop a broad scientific network and gain hands-on experience with complementary expertise and facilities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate you will be responsible for developing, validating and implementing computational tools for the stability assessment in collaboration with team members, supervisors and international collaborators.

In detail your responsibilities will include:

• Implement and benchmark simplified limit equilibrium methods against advanced computational modelling for dike instabilities
• Assess the reliability of simplified and advanced slope stability methods
• Characterise and map the uncertainty of the soil conditions in coastal dikes
• Evaluate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment
• Publish high-quality research in leading international journals and present findings at international conferences.
• Contribute to courses and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students

jobs.description:
DTU Nanolab is looking for experienced engineers and physicists within thin film deposition, thin film plasma etching and thin film characterization in its ISO 4 & 5 cleanroom for micro- and nanofabrication.

We are seeking process specialists for the process specialist team. The team is responsible for thin-film deposition equipment (PVD, CVD, thermal processing), plasma etching systems, and a large suite of characterization tools (AFM, SEM, XRD, XPS, EDX, optical and stylus profilers, ellipsometers, reflectometers, PL mappers, and more). Responsibilities span the full equipment lifecycle, from procurement and implementation to documentation, maintenance, troubleshooting and the development of in-depth tool and process expertise needed to support users throughout a system's lifetime. 

The job
We are seeking people with experience and interest in plasma etching (ICP, IBE), plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD), AFM, sputter deposition, RTP annealing, PE-ALD, XRD and photo spectrometry. The job includes

• Process development of new processes and maintenance of current processes
• Documentation, including user manuals and process documentation
• In charge of QC and calibration procedures 
• Helping, training and education of users
• Assisting in fault finding in cooperation with technicians
• Assisting in procurement of new equipment: Specifications, demo runs and run-in
• Networking with other cleanroom labs in Europe
You will work closely with other process specialists and technicians in the Process Group, as well as with other DTU Nanolab groups, researchers, students and engineers from DTU and commercial companies. A large part of your working day will be spent in ISO 4 and 5 cleanrooms, where you will wear a full cleanroom suit.

Our expectations of you
You must have a M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree within either engineering or physics within a relevant field (micro/nanofabrication, experimental physics or similar) and have knowledge and experimental skills within the area of either plasma etching or thin film deposition and within different relevant characterization tools. 

Furthermore, we expect you to possess skills and qualifications in one or more of these areas:

• Plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD) and other CVD techniques (ALD and LPCVD)
• Plasma etching (ICP etching)
• PVD techniques (sputter deposition, e-beam evaporation and thermal evaporation)
• Thermal processing (oxidation, annealing and rapid thermal annealing)
• Thin film characterization techniques (AFM, XRD, photo spectrometry and other relevant)
• Hands-on experience working in a cleanroom environment
• Have a broad understanding of micro and nano processing
• Have an eye for detail and work meticulously
• Work well in teams with people from different backgrounds
• Service-minded
• Self-driven and able to plan your own working day

Is able to respond quickly and effectively in emergency situations, including evacuation in case of alarms. Is able to perform tasks that require work while standing up and mobility for longer periods.

We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international work environment. The work is highly hands-on and with a large degree of variation. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. Please note that this is not a research position, but a technical position, with a main focus to facilitate academic and industrial users within the field of thin film processing and characterization.
